DescriptionTrim: To require intelligence community reporting on foreign fighter flow
DescriptionLLM: to and from terrorist safe havens abroad, and for other purposes. This bill directs the Director of National Intelligence (DNI) to submit to Congress a report on foreign fighter flows to and from terrorist safe havens abroad. DescriptionTrim: A bill entitled Prosecutorial Remedies and Other Tools
DescriptionLLM: to end the Exploitation of Children Today Act of 2003 or the PROTECT Act. Title I: Sanctions and Offenses - (Sec. 101) Amends the Federal criminal code to: (1) increase penalties for sexual exploitation of children; (2) establish a new offense for the production of child pornography; (3) increase penalties for child abduction and sex tourism; and (4) provide for civil remedies for personal injuries resulting from certain sex crimes against children. Title II: Investigations and Prosecutions - (Sec. 201) Authorizes appropriations for the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force. (Sec. 202) Directs the Attorney General to establish a National Internet Crimes Against Children Data System. Title III: Sentencing and Monitoring - (Sec. 301) Amends the Federal criminal code to: (1) increase penalties for repeat offenders of child exploitation crimes; and (2) establish mandatory minimum sentences for certain offenses. (Sec. 302) Directs the U.S. Sentencing Commission to review and amend Federal sentencing guidelines for child exploitation offenses. Title IV: Child Victims' Rights - (Sec. 401) Amends the Federal criminal code to provide for the rights of child victims and witnesses. Title V: Miscellaneous Provisions - (Sec. 501) Amends the Federal criminal code to provide for the forfeiture of property used in the commission of certain child exploitation offenses. (Sec. 502) Directs the Attorney General to report to Congress on the implementation of this Act.
Description: to end the Exploitation of Children Today Act of 2003.

DescriptionTrim: To amend title 38, United States Code, to improve the opportunity for veterans
DescriptionLLM: to use their educational benefits, and for other purposes. This bill directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to disapprove courses of education provided by public institutions of higher learning (IHLs) that charge veterans living in the state higher tuition and fees than in-state residents. The bill also requires the VA to disapprove courses of education provided by public IHLs that do not provide priority enrollment for veterans. Additionally, the bill extends the time period during which veterans can use their educational benefits from 15 years to the entirety of their lives. The bill also includes provisions to improve the transition assistance program for veterans, enhance the vocational rehabilitation and employment program, and provide additional support for veterans pursuing science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) degrees.

DescriptionLLM: tevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act to improve the conservation of sharks. Directs the Secretary of Commerce to identify nations whose fishing vessels are engaged, or have been engaged during the preceding calendar year, in fishing activities or practices that target or incidentally catch sharks and are not subject to a regulatory program for the conservation of sharks that is comparable to that of the United States, taking into account different conditions. Requires the Secretary to initiate consultations with such nations to encourage the implementation of measures to conserve sharks. Authorizes the Secretary to establish a procedure to certify whether such nations have adopted and are effectively enforcing a regulatory program for the conservation of sharks.
